requirements.title: Records at or below the gate stay inline
requirements.statement: A heap record whose serialized size does not exceed the OOS inline target is stored entirely inline: no attribute is demoted, HAS_OOS stays clear, and a class that has never demoted a value has no OOS file.

citation.source: §1 Trigger Conditions — Largest-First Demotion (CBRD-26776; physical target CBRD-27057), step 1 (record gate)

authority.note: Assertable only where the pinned gate (DB_PAGESIZE/4) and the normative four-record target agree. Schema-A BIT VARYING N ≤ 939 / 1,963 / 4,011 (4/8/16 KiB) stays inline under both; the band above is OOS-REP-03.

requirements.pinned_observation: Pinned gate 1,014 / 2,038 / 4,086 B versus normative 988 / 2,012 / 4,060 B (ticket 11 §5.1). No OOS file is created until the first demotion (Has_oos_file 0).

requirements.title: Largest-first demotion above the gate
requirements.statement: When a record exceeds the OOS inline target, eligible variable values are demoted one at a time in descending size until the record is at or below the target or candidates are exhausted; smaller eligible values may remain inline, and every value reads back exactly.

citation.source: §1 Trigger Conditions — Largest-First Demotion (CBRD-26776; physical target CBRD-27057), step 3 (largest-first loop)

authority.note: Assertable above both gates (schema-A N ≥ 964 / 1,988 / 4,036). The number of demoted values is observable per class through SHOW HEAP OOS chunk counts on an isolated table; per-attribute placement needs a paired debug or instrumented run. At the pin the SQL INSERT path writes no oos.log line (ticket 11 §6).

requirements.pinned_observation: Order and early stop implemented in heap_attrinfo_determine_disk_layout; the stop compares against the pinned gate, not the normative target.
attack_dimensions: two unequal eligible columns (only the largest demoted)
over-demotion by one value near a VOT width boundary (conservative estimate)

requirements.title: Four-record physical target (CBRD-27057)
requirements.statement: The record gate and the demotion stop use the PG-style four-record physical target derived from heap_nonheader_page_capacity(), excluding heap unfill: 988 / 2,012 / 4,060 B at 4 / 8 / 16 KiB.

citation.source: CBRD-27057 four-record physical target — spec note (2026-07-13) and §1 Trigger Conditions — Largest-First Demotion (CBRD-26776; physical target CBRD-27057)

authority.note: Accepted design absent at the pin. Cases in the disputed band take the UNSUPPORTED outcome; their engine output is retained as evidence and never promoted to an answer. Ticket 11 recorded this as a Capability gap of the pinned engine.

requirements.pinned_observation: heap_file.c:12350 and :12383 compare against DB_PAGESIZE / 4; heap_oos_inline_target_size does not exist. Disputed band schema-A N in [940, 963] / [1,964, 1,987] / [4,012, 4,035] stays inline at the pin.
attack_dimensions: both sides of the normative boundary at each page size

requirements.title: Eligibility floor where pinned and normative agree
requirements.statement: A variable value whose serialized size is at or below 16 B is never demoted, and a variable value whose serialized size exceeds 24 B is a demotion candidate whenever its record exceeds the gate.

citation.source: §1 Trigger Conditions — Largest-First Demotion (CBRD-26776; physical target CBRD-27057), step 2 (eligibility)

authority.note: Both floors agree outside the [17, 24] B serialized band. For BIT VARYING that is logical N ≤ 15 (never demoted) and N ≥ 24 (candidate). The band N in [16, 23] is OOS-REP-05.

requirements.pinned_observation: 15-byte value stays inline; 16-, 23- and 24-byte values are demoted (Oos_recs_sumlen 36 / 40 / 44). Normatively only the 24-byte value may be demoted.
attack_dimensions: fixed BIT column pushes the record over the gate so only the small variable value is a candidate

requirements.title: 24-byte identity layout (CBRD-26950)
requirements.statement: The OOS inline stub is 24 bytes (head OOS OID, full length, packed identity stamp), each chunk header is 24 bytes with a raw LOG_LSA stamp captured under the write latch, the eligibility floor is strictly greater than 24 B, and deletes are identity-checked against the stamp.

citation.source: CBRD-26950 identity layout — Identity layout reconciliation (2026-09-09), §2 Record Binary Layout and §2 Multi-Chunk OOS Chain

authority.note: Accepted design absent at the pin (PR #7695 unmerged). Physical expectations that depend on the 24-byte layout are withheld; their cases take the UNSUPPORTED outcome. Universal value-correctness checks continue under OOS-CL-04.

requirements.accepted_design: CBRD-26950 identity layout (24-byte stub and chunk header, identity-checked delete)
requirements.pinned_observation: OR_OOS_INLINE_SIZE = 16 (object_representation.h:466); oos_record_header is 16 B (oos_file.hpp:28-33); oos_delete takes no expected identity. Boundaries shift by 8 B: single-chunk max 16,288 pinned vs 16,280 normative at 16 KiB; eligibility band N in [16, 23] demoted at the pin.
attack_dimensions: single-to-multi chunk boundary under a 24-byte header
OOS + bigone rejection threshold under a 24-byte stub
stamp uniqueness across slot reuse with logging enabled

requirements.title: Type-agnostic eligibility including LOB locators (ADR-0002)
requirements.statement: Eligibility depends only on the value being variable-length and larger than the floor; BLOB/CLOB locator values demote like any other variable value with LOB copy semantics preserved, and deleting or vacuuming a demoted locator never removes the external LOB payload.

citation.source: ADR-0002 BLOB/CLOB locator columns remain OOS-demotable (type-agnostic eligibility)

authority.note: Whole-value equality per type. String types are compressed and unsuitable for size boundaries; use them for correctness, not for boundary arithmetic.

attack_dimensions: BIT VARYING, VARCHAR (compressed and uncompressed), VARNCHAR, JSON, SET/MULTISET/SEQUENCE, BLOB/CLOB locators
INSERT ... SELECT copying of LOB rows
stub-writer S_DOESNT_FIT retry after locator size drift

requirements.title: Multi-chunk value chains
requirements.statement: A value larger than one page's maximum single-chunk payload is stored as a chain of chunk records, inserted tail first, and is read back complete and byte-identical; total_data_length excludes every chunk header.

citation.source: §2 Multi-Chunk OOS Chain

authority.note: Assert value equality and, on an isolated table, the chunk count from SHOW HEAP OOS. The exact split boundary is pinned-layout specific (16-byte header); the normative 24-byte boundary is OOS-REP-05.

requirements.pinned_observation: Largest single-chunk N = 3,995 / 8,091 / 16,283; two chunks from N = 3,996 / 8,092 / 16,284 (Oos_num_recs 2, Oos_num_user_pages 3).
attack_dimensions: one byte either side of the split
mixed single- and multi-chunk values in one table
distinct byte pattern per chunk to detect cross-row mixing

requirements.title: OOS + bigone rejection (CBRD-26937)
requirements.statement: An INSERT or UPDATE whose record would still exceed heap_Maxslotted_reclength after demotion while containing an OOS inline stub is rejected with ER_HEAP_OOS_OVERPASS_MAXOBJ_SIZE before any chunk is written; no row is stored and no OOS value chain is created. A non-OOS bigone record, or an OOS-backed record left between the target and the bigone threshold, succeeds.

citation.source: §1 OOS + bigone Rejection (CBRD-26937)

authority.note: Assert the rejection, the absence of the row and the absence of an OOS file or new chunks. Expected-error answers use the pinned error code and message text (ticket 11 §4 g); the context's -1375 is drift, reported to the context maintainer.

requirements.pinned_observation: Error code is -1382 at the pin (error_code.h:1782); message reports 'size (N bytes) still exceeds the maximum record size (M bytes)'. Schema B: largest accepted F = 3,888 / 7,984 / 16,176; smallest rejected F = 3,889 / 7,985 / 16,177 with a 16-byte stub.
attack_dimensions: fixed BIT(n) plus one OOS-backed column
UPDATE that grows a fixed column past the threshold

requirements.title: NULL and empty eligible values
requirements.statement: A NULL or zero-length value in an OOS-eligible column is never demoted and reads back as NULL or as the empty value.

citation.source: §1 Trigger Conditions — Largest-First Demotion (CBRD-26776; physical target CBRD-27057), step 2 (eligibility)

authority.note: Follows from eligibility requiring a serialized size above the floor. Assert on records that otherwise exceed the gate so demotion of siblings is exercised.

attack_dimensions: empty BIT VARYING and empty VARCHAR beside demoted siblings

requirements.title: Many OOS-backed attributes in one record
requirements.statement: A record may carry many OOS inline stubs (ten or more); HAS_OOS is set once, each demoted attribute's VOT entry carries IS_OOS, and every value reads back exactly.

citation.source: §2 Record Binary Layout

authority.note: Flags are observable only through debug or diagnostic channels; the SQL seam asserts values and chunk counts. An OOS-bearing record never reaches 4-byte VOT entries (structural exclusion, ticket 11 §5.1).

requirements.title: Inline and OOS transitions across writes
requirements.statement: An attribute's representation may move between inline and OOS on each INSERT or UPDATE as the record size crosses the target; the logical value is never affected by the transition.

citation.source: §1 Trigger Conditions — Largest-First Demotion (CBRD-26776; physical target CBRD-27057)

authority.note: Assert values across grow/shrink sequences; placement changes are evidence, not the oracle.

attack_dimensions: grow a value past the gate then shrink it below
change a sibling so a previously inline value becomes the largest candidate

requirements.title: Placement hints: logical correctness only
requirements.statement: With STORAGE PREFER_INLINE or STORAGE FORCE_OUTLINE declared on a column, values read back exactly, DDL and DML error paths behave, and the record stays valid; where a value is placed is recorded as an implementation observation.

citation.source: §5 Proposed Design Discussions — Per-column inline preference (CBRD-26912, proposed)

authority.note: Ticket 10 policy 2: implemented behavior without established acceptance gets logical-correctness and error-path tests; placement is observed, never asserted. Coverage scope is a pending decision request from ticket 11 §9.

requirements.pinned_observation: Grammar accepts both hints (csql_grammar.y:10574-10582); FORCE_OUTLINE bypasses the record gate (a 40-byte value in a small record was demoted).
attack_dimensions: hint on a column that is not variable-length (error path)
ALTER adding and removing the hint

requirements.title: Placement-hint policy authority
requirements.statement: Whether PREFER_INLINE ordering and the FORCE_OUTLINE gate bypass are required behavior is undecided; no placement expectation is fixed for either hint.

citation.source: §5 Proposed Design Discussions — Per-column inline preference (CBRD-26912, proposed)

authority.note: Source existence does not establish acceptance (ticket 10). The gap stays visible in the matrix and does not block OOS-REP-12.

requirements.authority_question: Is CBRD-26912 (STORAGE PREFER_INLINE) accepted, and is STORAGE FORCE_OUTLINE an accepted design at all? If accepted, what exact ordering and bypass semantics are required?
requirements.pinned_observation: Both hints implemented beyond accepted policy (ticket 11 §4 b).

requirements.title: Stub-size terminology: 16, 20 or 24 bytes
requirements.statement: Residual context statements still give the profitable demotion threshold as strictly greater than 16 B (§5 Limitations row for CBRD-26776) while the accepted layout fixes the OOS inline stub, chunk header and floor at 24 B, and the invariants research met a 20-byte generation-stub draft; the single normative size must be confirmed.

citation.source: §5 Limitations (Milestone 1) — Bulk-externalize row (profitable threshold wording)

authority.note: Mixed-era statement from the invariants research (stub-size terminology). Expectations in the 17-24 B serialized band are withheld (OOS-REP-05); outside the band OOS-REP-04 applies.

requirements.authority_question: Confirm that every remaining 16-byte and 20-byte statement is historical, that 24 B is the single normative stub, chunk-header and floor size, and that the pinned 16-byte constant is a conformance gap rather than an alternative accepted layout.
requirements.pinned_observation: OR_OOS_INLINE_SIZE = 16 and a 16-byte chunk header at the pin (ticket 11 §4 d, e).

requirements.title: INSERT then SELECT returns the exact value
requirements.statement: An inserted OOS-backed row reads back with every attribute byte-identical to the inserted value, for single rows and bulk inserts of varying sizes.

citation.source: §3 INSERT

authority.note: Exact whole-value equality justified before the engine runs; DISK_SIZE supports the arithmetic but is not a placement oracle. Pair with activation evidence.

requirements.title: UPDATE correctness
requirements.statement: After an UPDATE of an OOS-backed attribute, or of an inline attribute in an OOS-backed record, the updater and every later reader see the exact new value; repeated updates leave the final value correct.

citation.source: §3 UPDATE (Always New OID — M1)

authority.note: Universal value correctness independent of the physical design; chain ownership is OOS-SQL-03 and OOS-SQL-04.

attack_dimensions: UPDATE of only an inline attribute
UPDATE with subquery reading the same OOS value

requirements.title: M1 always-new-chain on UPDATE (current behavior)
requirements.statement: At the pin every UPDATE allocates fresh OOS value chains and head OOS OIDs for the new record version, even for attributes the statement did not assign.

citation.source: §3 UPDATE (Always New OID — M1) — Current implementation

authority.note: Historical and current-implementation behavior superseded on paper by CBRD-27230. Record chunk-count growth as an observation; never promote it as required behavior (scenario 2.2 wording is M1-era).

requirements.pinned_observation: heap_attrinfo_insert_to_oos always allocates fresh chains; the vacuum forward-walk relies on old/new head-OID disjointness.
attack_dimensions: UPDATE of an inline attribute only

requirements.title: UPDATE chain reuse and commit-conditional cleanup (CBRD-27230)
requirements.statement: UPDATE reuses the OOS value chains of attributes the statement does not assign; dropped chains are announced by a commit-conditional RVOOS_NOTIFY_VACUUM record consumed by vacuum; the forward-walk is removed; DELETE and the SA_MODE eager path are unchanged.

citation.source: CBRD-27230 UPDATE chain reuse — spec note (2026-08-13) and §3 UPDATE superseding ownership invariant

authority.note: Accepted design absent at the pin. Reuse and notify-record expectations are withheld; rollback-survival correctness continues under OOS-CL-03.

requirements.accepted_design: CBRD-27230 UPDATE chain reuse with RVOOS_NOTIFY_VACUUM cleanup
requirements.pinned_observation: Forward walk present (vacuum_oos.cpp:154, :275); no notify emitter (recovery.c:899, mvcc.h:268 reserve the record).
attack_dimensions: unassigned attribute keeps its head OID

requirements.title: DELETE semantics
requirements.statement: A deleted OOS-backed row is gone for the deleter and for later readers; the deleted record keeps its stubs and its value chains are not removed at delete time in MVCC mode, so the table stays reusable and earlier snapshots can still read the value.

citation.source: §3 DELETE

authority.note: Logical checks on the SQL seam; 'chains not removed at delete time' is assertable through SHOW HEAP OOS chunk counts in client-server mode only, because the standalone eager path deletes synchronously (ticket 11 §6).

requirements.pinned_observation: Standalone DELETE dropped Oos_num_recs to 0 immediately while pages stayed allocated (LSA-gate deferral).
requirements.configuration_scope: Physical deferral applies to client-server (MVCC) mode; standalone mode deletes eagerly.
attack_dimensions: DELETE with WHERE on an OOS column

requirements.title: Transaction atomicity and undo correctness
requirements.statement: ROLLBACK, savepoint rollback and statement failure restore the previous record as-is, including its OOS inline stubs whose head OIDs still reference live chains; no partial effect and no orphan chain remains from the aborted work.

citation.source: §4 Recovery & Replication Invariants, invariant 2 (Undo correctness)

authority.note: Exact original values after rollback; constraint and trigger failures are the statement-failure dimension. Orphan-chain cleanup eventuality is OOS-CL-02.

attack_dimensions: UPDATE of an OOS-backed attribute then ROLLBACK
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT across OOS writes
unique/PK/NOT NULL violation on an OOS row
trigger raising an error after an OOS write

requirements.title: Deferred-reuse text versus the accepted CBRD-27230 design
requirements.statement: §5 Optimization Ideas A and the Milestones section still describe UPDATE value-chain reuse as a cancelled-M3 future improvement not in M2, while the 2026-08-13 spec note records CBRD-27230 as an accepted design and M2 as the umbrella for all remaining OOS work; whether reuse is a merge-gating conformance item is undecided.

citation.source: §5 Optimization Ideas — A. Update OOS value-chain reuse (CBRD-26516) and Milestones (M3 cancelled)

authority.note: Mixed-era statement from the invariants research (deferred reuse text). Decides whether OOS-SQL-04's UNSUPPORTED status is a merge gate or accepted later-milestone work; either way the pin's behavior is never promoted as the answer.

requirements.authority_question: Is CBRD-27230 UPDATE chain reuse required for feat/oos conformance before merge, or deferred to a later milestone? Should Optimization Idea A and the M3 milestone text be rewritten to point at the accepted design?

requirements.title: Every read path returns the complete OOS value
requirements.statement: Every SQL read path that consumes an OOS-backed attribute obtains the complete OOS value: heap scans, index scans, joins, prepared statements, aggregates and functions, constraint and trigger evaluation, and attribute-level reads that touch one column.

citation.source: §3 SELECT (OOS Resolve)

authority.note: Exact whole-value equality per path; operation success alone does not prove Resolve routing, so pair each path with activation evidence where the path is claimed as OOS coverage.

attack_dimensions: index scan on a non-OOS key projecting the OOS column
join on inline keys projecting OOS values from both sides
GROUP BY / aggregate over OOS values
constraint and trigger reading the OOS value
SELECT of only the inline columns (no OOS I/O expected; observation)

requirements.title: Old-version reads reconstruct through undo stubs
requirements.statement: A reader whose snapshot predates another session's UPDATE or DELETE reads the exact old value, reconstructed through prev_version_lsa, the undo record's stubs and oos_read, whether the writer is uncommitted or committed.

citation.source: §4 Recovery & Replication Invariants, invariant 2 (Undo correctness)

authority.note: Needs two sessions with acknowledged barriers (ticket 05). Value survival is the oracle; cleanup afterwards is OOS-CL-02.

attack_dimensions: uncommitted UPDATE visible only to the updater
committed UPDATE with an earlier reader snapshot
deleted row still visible to an earlier snapshot

requirements.title: Raw-byte consumers receive expanded records (ADR-0003)
requirements.statement: Every path that consumes raw record bytes (client copy-area fetch, unloaddb, compactdb, partition redistribution, catalog updates, re-insertion into another heap) receives fully expanded records; no OOS inline stub leaks to an OOS-unaware consumer.

citation.source: ADR-0003 OOS record expansion is opt-in for raw-byte consumers

authority.note: Assert logical output of each consumer (unload file contents, compacted table values, moved partition rows). CBRD-26948 is an expected finding to re-verify at the pin, not to assume.

requirements.pinned_observation: locator_sr.c:2337 expands copy-area records at the pin (research report); unloaddb/compactdb leak status unverified.
attack_dimensions: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT / INSERT ... SELECT

requirements.title: OOS file lifecycle: at most one per heap, removed with the heap
requirements.statement: Each heap file has at most one OOS file, lazily created on first demotion and recorded in the heap header; destroying the heap (DROP TABLE, and TRUNCATE which recreates the heap) leaves no orphan OOS file.

citation.source: §4 Recovery & Replication Invariants, invariant 6 (OOS file <-> heap file 1:1)

authority.note: Observable through SHOW HEAP OOS (Has_oos_file) and diagdb -d 1 / -d 2 owner descriptors. The DROP cleanup is the resolved CBRD-26608 design; the context has no explicit TRUNCATE sentence, so the TRUNCATE expectation is derived from invariant 6 and noted as such.

requirements.pinned_observation: FILE_OOS owner descriptor 'CLASS_OID … OOS for HFID …' printed by diagdb -d 1 at the pin.
attack_dimensions: DROP TABLE with single- and multi-chunk values
DROP concurrent with checkdb (narrow race noted in §5; observation)

requirements.title: Schema evolution preserves OOS values
requirements.statement: After ALTER TABLE (add, drop, modify or rename a column, change a type, add or drop an index, partition changes) every OOS-backed value reads back exactly and the resulting records are valid.

citation.source: §3 SELECT (OOS Resolve)

authority.note: Universal value correctness across rewrites; the rewrite side applies the write rules of OOS-REP-02.

attack_dimensions: ADD COLUMN with default beside OOS values
DROP COLUMN of an OOS-backed column
MODIFY type of an OOS-backed column
ADD INDEX on inline key of an OOS table

requirements.title: loaddb writes correct OOS-backed rows, including no-logging mode
requirements.statement: Rows loaded with loaddb read back exactly; with logging disabled the values remain correct while stamp-uniqueness and recovery guarantees are not asserted, per the accepted no-logging exception.

citation.source: §2 Multi-Chunk OOS Chain — Accepted logging policy (2026-09-09)

authority.note: Assert values in both modes; recovery after a no-logging load is recorded as observation only.

attack_dimensions: loaddb of an unloaded OOS table

requirements.title: compactdb and checkdb on OOS tables
requirements.statement: checkdb passes on a consistent database holding OOS files, and compactdb preserves every OOS-backed value; utility exit status is asserted explicitly.

citation.source: ADR-0003 OOS record expansion is opt-in for raw-byte consumers

authority.note: Utility exit status plus value equality after the utility; the private DROP-reclaim pattern (extract identifier, fail explicitly) is the model.

requirements.title: backup and restore preserve OOS values
requirements.statement: A database restored from a full or incremental backup returns every committed OOS-backed value exactly and its OOS files remain consistent (checkdb passes).

citation.source: §4 Recovery & Replication Invariants, invariant 1 (WAL completeness)

authority.note: Durability of committed state through the backup path; assert values and checkdb exit status.

attack_dimensions: backup of an encrypted OOS database (with OOS-OPS-04)

requirements.title: Space accounting of OOS files (CBRD-27350)
requirements.statement: spacedb and diagdb output for OOS storage is recorded as observed: at the pin OOS files are folded into the HEAP category and attributed to classes only through diagdb owner descriptors.

citation.source: §5 Known Bugs — spacedb/diagdb can't see OOS space

authority.note: QA tooling ask, not required OOS behavior; record what the tools print so the expected finding CBRD-27350 stays visible.

requirements.pinned_observation: spacedb -S -p reports 53 heap files where 45 are heaps and 8 are OOS files (ticket 11 §6).
attack_dimensions: spacedb totals before and after OOS inserts

requirements.title: Snapshot survival across update, delete and vacuum
requirements.statement: A reader that established its snapshot by a real read keeps reading the exact old value while another session updates or deletes the row and vacuum runs; the old value is never lost before the reader releases.

citation.source: §4 Vacuum + OOS (IMPLEMENTED — CBRD-26668, PR #6986 merged)

authority.note: Schedule family 'snapshot survival' (ticket 05) with acknowledged barriers and observed vacuum progress. Value survival is the oracle here; post-release cleanup is OOS-CL-02.

requirements.title: Dead-version chains are reclaimed by vacuum once no reader needs them
requirements.statement: The OOS value chains owned by dead record versions are deleted by vacuum after every snapshot that could read them has ended; no chain is deleted earlier and no chain is permanently orphaned.

citation.source: §4 Vacuum + OOS (IMPLEMENTED — CBRD-26668, PR #6986 merged)

authority.note: Assert chunk-count decrease only after proving eligibility (no active snapshot older than the delete) and safety (vacuum processed the block, observed progress). Before eligibility, a decrease is a failure candidate; after eligibility, absence of decrease within the bounded wait is a failure candidate.

attack_dimensions: UPDATE old chain reclaimed after reader release

requirements.title: Rollback survival against vacuum (CBRD-27237)
requirements.statement: After an UPDATE of an OOS-backed attribute is rolled back, the restored value remains exact after vacuum has processed the aborted transaction's log records.

citation.source: §4 Recovery & Replication Invariants, invariant 2 (Undo correctness)

authority.note: Universal rollback correctness independent of the physical design; expected to FAIL at the pin as Engine defect CBRD-27237. A documented Engine defect still records the FAIL outcome.

requirements.pinned_observation: Forward-walk acts on undo-image content with no commit/abort filter (analysis-based, no runtime repro recorded in the context).

requirements.title: Live data survives slot reuse and vacuum retry (CBRD-26950)
requirements.statement: After vacuum frees an OOS slot and another row's chain reuses that slot, a vacuum retry (worker pause, mid-block error or crash recovery re-running the block) never deletes the new owner's chunk; the complete value survives.

citation.source: §4 Vacuum + OOS (IMPLEMENTED — CBRD-26668, PR #6986 merged)

authority.note: Universal correctness (vacuum never deletes live data); expected to FAIL at the pin as Engine defect CBRD-26950. The identity-stamp mechanism itself is OOS-REP-05 (UNSUPPORTED).

requirements.pinned_observation: oos_chunk_exists checks occupied, not mine; header has no identity stamp.
attack_dimensions: prove reclamation and reuse of the targeted slot

requirements.title: Empty-page reclaim invariant (CBRD-26786)
requirements.statement: Every fully emptied OOS data page is eventually returned to the file manager, and an OOS file reserves a new sector only when no safely reclaimable empty page exists; pages whose last writer may still be a live undo source are deferred, and deferral ends when that writer finishes.

citation.source: CBRD-26786 empty-page reclaim invariant — spec note (2026-08-28) and §4 Vacuum + OOS

authority.note: Ticket 10 policy 3: assert page release only after proving the page is empty, is a data page (not the header page), belongs to a non-legacy file, and passes the LSA gate (no active writer). Never use an unconditional zero-page assertion. Ticket 11 found the mechanisms present at the pin (conforming).

requirements.pinned_observation: oos_reclaim_lsa_gate_passes, oos_reclaim_empty_pages, oos_reclaim_sweep_step and oos_alloc_page_with_reclaim exist at the pin; after a standalone DELETE, Oos_num_user_pages stayed at 2 (deferral).
attack_dimensions: empty page with active deleter, then abort
interrupted sweep and boot-rule lap after crash
growth-gate sweep at the single growth point

requirements.title: No unjustified OOS file growth under churn
requirements.statement: Under sustained insert/delete churn with reclaimable empty pages available, the OOS file does not reserve new sectors while a safely reclaimable page exists.

citation.source: CBRD-26786 empty-page reclaim invariant — spec note (2026-08-28) and §4 Vacuum + OOS

authority.note: Progress witness: page counts from SHOW HEAP OOS over time with eligibility established; the bound on 'eventually' is a Specification gap (OOS-CL-07) so the case records the observed lag rather than asserting a fixed bound.

attack_dimensions: steady-state churn at each page size
churn with a long-lived reader deferring pages

requirements.title: Reclamation domain and eventuality bound
requirements.statement: The exact domain of 'every fully emptied OOS data page is eventually returned' is not fixed: the header page, legacy numerable files, safely deferred pages and the time bound of 'eventually' need authoritative wording.

citation.source: CBRD-26786 empty-page reclaim invariant — spec note (2026-08-28) and §4 Vacuum + OOS

authority.note: Mixed-era statement from the invariants research (unconditional reclamation). Until answered, physical page-count expectations are withheld except where eligibility and safety are proven per OOS-CL-05.

requirements.authority_question: Which pages are inside the reclaim guarantee (data pages only; header page excluded; legacy numerable files excluded?), and what progress witness or time bound makes 'eventually' testable? Is an implementation's sticky-page or legacy-file exception an accepted specification exception?

requirements.title: Chain ownership wording: no cross-version sharing versus borrowed references
requirements.statement: The Writing Conventions still require stating that value chains are never shared across record versions, while the accepted CBRD-27230 ownership invariant allows older versions to hold borrowed references; which statement governs at the pin is undecided.

citation.source: Writing Conventions — ownership statement

authority.note: Mixed-era statement from the invariants research. Ownership assertions are withheld; value correctness continues under OOS-CL-01 and OOS-CL-03.

requirements.authority_question: Which ownership statement is normative at the pin, and should the Writing Conventions be updated to the superseding invariant with an explicit 'effective once implemented' qualifier?

requirements.title: Cancellation and disconnect during OOS writes
requirements.statement: A statement cancelled or a session disconnected during an OOS INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE leaves no partial effect: the transaction is rolled back, values of other rows are intact, and the aborted work's chains become eligible for cleanup.

citation.source: §4 Recovery & Replication Invariants, invariant 2 (Undo correctness)

authority.note: Assert transaction state and values; cleanup eventuality per OOS-CL-02.

attack_dimensions: kill the client mid multi-chunk INSERT

requirements.title: Concurrent DDL against OOS DML
requirements.statement: ALTER, DROP or TRUNCATE running concurrently with OOS reads and writes yields either exact values or the standard DDL/lock error; no crash, no stub leak and no corrupted value.

requirements.title: TDE covers OOS pages (CBRD-26830)
requirements.statement: For a TDE-encrypted class, OOS pages hold no plaintext payload on disk (data volumes, log, backup); a lazily created OOS file inherits the class algorithm before its VFID is published; altering encryption applies to an existing OOS file; decrypted reads return exact values.

citation.source: CBRD-26830 TDE plaintext leak on OOS pages (security) — listed in Quick Reference › JIRA; fix recorded as DONE on feat/oos in §5 Known Bugs (commit 138f624964)

authority.note: The normative context has no encryption section. The requirement rests on CUBRID's general TDE guarantee applied to the OOS file as part of the class's storage (invariant 6) and on the resolved security defect CBRD-26830, whose fix on feat/oos is an accepted decision that plaintext OOS pages of an encrypted class are a defect. Combine ciphertext evidence (recognizable non-compressible payload absent from raw pages) with correct decrypted reads and proof that the targeted pages were written. A request that the context maintainer add an explicit TDE-on-OOS statement is recorded in the catalogue's context notes.
